title: read through a pointer st_realloc invalidated by moving the object
object: a, 24 bytes, grown to 4096 by st_realloc, which frees the old block when it moves
control: reads through the pointer st_realloc returned

requires.why: st_realloc must have succeeded AND moved the object. An allocator that returns NULL (the arena, currently) or grows in place has no stale pointer and no defect.

note: The shape of SQLite's agginfo defect (capstone case 01) and of PostgreSQL's repalloc rows: no free() appears in the source, which is why it survives code review.

asan.why: On malloc realloc's old block goes to the quarantine. The arena has no realloc at all. A free list that copies must poison the old block in its own realloc for the annotated arm to work.

valgrind.why: As above, with MEMPOOL_FREE on the old block.

hwasan.why: malloc retags the old block; no CMA interface for the others.

ubsan.why: -fsanitize=bounds needs a statically known array bound; a pointer out of an allocator has none. The row is kept so the report can say UBSan is not a heap tool rather than leaving it out.

lowfat.why: LowFat checks bounds only; it has no notion of a lifetime.

status: written, smoke-run on malloc and arena; server run pending (A5)
